scope.q: What specific types of information (e.g., technical specs, HR policies, marketing assets) are most critical for employees to find quickly, and how frequently do they need to access it?
scope.why: Understanding the high-value information types and access patterns helps prioritize data sources and search relevance criteria.

scope.q: What are the current pain points beyond just 'not finding anything,' such as specific search failures, time wasted, or critical decisions delayed due to lack of information?
scope.why: Identifying concrete negative impacts helps quantify the problem and define success metrics beyond simple search functionality.

scope.q: Are there any existing access control mechanisms or data sensitivity requirements (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) that must be maintained when centralizing or indexing this information?
scope.why: Data security and compliance are non-negotiable and will heavily influence architecture, indexing, and display of search results.

decomposition.title: Data Source Connectors & Indexing
decomposition.why: This piece focuses on robustly extracting and processing data from disparate, unstructured sources.

decomposition.title: Search & Retrieval Service
decomposition.why: This subproblem is dedicated to the core search logic, query processing, and result ranking.

decomposition.title: User Interface & Experience
decomposition.why: This covers how users interact with the search system and consume the results effectively.

decomposition.title: Access Control & Permissions Sync
decomposition.why: Ensuring users only see information they are authorized to access is a critical, standalone security concern.

decomposition.title: Monitoring & Analytics
decomposition.why: This is crucial for understanding system performance, user behavior, and identifying areas for improvement.

sprint.title: Core Search Service & Basic Indexing
sprint.deliv: HTTP endpoint that accepts a query and returns dummy results from a hardcoded list.

sprint.title: Confluence Connector & Initial Indexing
sprint.deliv: Service that connects to Confluence API, extracts page titles and content, and populates a local index (e.g., Elasticsearch).

sprint.title: Basic Search UI & Result Display
sprint.deliv: Web page with a search bar that submits queries to the search service and displays actual indexed Confluence results.

sprint.title: Google Drive Connector & Indexing
sprint.deliv: Service to connect to Google Drive API, extract file metadata and text content, and integrate into the search index.

sprint.title: Access Control Integration (Confluence)
sprint.deliv: Search results for Confluence content are filtered based on the querying user's Confluence permissions.

sprint.title: Result Ranking & Relevance Tuning
sprint.deliv: Implement basic ranking algorithms (e.g., TF-IDF, freshness) and allow configuration of relevance boosters.

sprint.title: Deployment & Basic Monitoring
sprint.deliv: System deployed to staging environment with basic uptime and error logging for all services and connectors.

risks.risk: Poor data quality or inconsistent formatting across sources will lead to irrelevant search results.
risks.mitigation: Implement a data profiling step during connector development to identify common data issues and build robust pre-processing pipelines to normalize content before indexing.

risks.risk: Complex or granular access control requirements across different platforms may be difficult to replicate accurately in the search service.
risks.mitigation: Start with a simplified access model (e.g., 'if you can access the source, you can see the result') and iteratively add more granular permissions, leveraging native platform APIs where possible, with a dedicated ACL sync service.

risks.risk: Users may not adopt the new search tool if it doesn't provide a significantly better experience than existing fragmented methods.
risks.mitigation: Conduct user interviews early and frequently to gather feedback on UI, search relevance, and desired features, iterating on the design based on their input.

risks.risk: Legacy systems (like the 'very old wiki') may lack APIs or structured access for data extraction, making integration difficult or impossible.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize connectors for systems with known APIs. For the old wiki, investigate manual export options or consider a one-time migration to a supported platform if direct integration is infeasible.
